applies_when: learner gives one root of a two-root quadratic

dbe_source.recommendation: Candidates gave only one root when the question had two. A quadratic equation has two solutions. Both must be written, joined by 'or'.

lesson.concept: A quadratic equation has TWO roots, not one. If you write only one, you have not finished the question. Both roots must be written, joined by 'or'.
lesson.why: In (x - a)(x - b) = 0, you must set each factor to zero. Setting only one factor to zero gives only one root and loses the mark for the second.

work: Do not stop after the first root.

probe.hint: Two factors. Two roots. Write both with 'or' between them.

learner_message: You gave one root. A quadratic has two. The second one is missing.
